task: Write one sentence of your own using the word profligate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know profligate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The startup was profligate from day one, leasing three floors it never filled and catering breakfast for a staff of nine.
Free-spending stops short of profligate — the free-spending pick up every check and enjoy it; nothing is yet being ruined.
Extravagant stops short of profligate — extravagance buys too much, while profligacy pours the whole fortune out and calls for more.

Wasteful is the everyday, neutral word for using more than a task needs — long showers, lights left burning. Profligate raises waste to an indictment: value poured away headlong, past caring, with a hint of vice. A habit is wasteful; a squandered fortune is profligate.

Prodigal means wastefully lavish with what was given — the runaway who burns through the inheritance. The word mourns the waste more than it blames. Profligate turns the same squandering into an accusation, adding the note of moral abandon that prodigal's sad story lacks.
